tools.name: login
tools.description: Authenticate this server and persist the key to ~/.test-lab/config.json (the same file the testlab CLI uses). Pass apiKey to store a key directly, or omit it to run the browser device-code flow (a browser window opens for you to approve). Pass profile to store the key under a named account (so several clients coexist without overwriting each other) - the account you log into becomes this session's active one. Usually unnecessary if TESTLAB_API_KEY is set in the server env or you've already run `testlab login`.

apiKey.description: A tl_... API key to store directly (skips the browser flow).

profile.description: Name this account (e.g. "acme"). Omit to use the "default" profile. See list_profiles / switch_profile.

force.description: Re-authenticate, or overwrite a profile pointing at a different account.

tools.name: list_profiles
tools.description: List the accounts stored in ~/.test-lab/config.json and which one is active right now (session override, env, a .test-lab.json in the working folder, or the config default). Use switch_profile to change accounts.

tools.name: switch_profile
tools.description: Act as a different stored account for subsequent tool calls. The switch is session-scoped by default; set persistDefault to also make it the config default, or bindFolder to write a ./.test-lab.json in the server's working directory so future sessions in that folder pick it up automatically.

profile.description: The stored profile name to switch to (see list_profiles).

persistDefault.description: Also set this as the global default profile in the config.

bindFolder.description: Also bind the working folder to this profile via ./.test-lab.json (no key stored).

tools.name: whoami
tools.description: Show the account this server is authenticated as (email, account type, plan) and its test-plan count.

tools.name: list_test_plans
tools.description: List the account's test plans (id, name, labels, pre-steps).

tools.name: create_test_plan
tools.description: Create one natural-language test plan. The target URL lives IN the prompt. Use the `examples` tool for the full field reference. Reference secrets as {{credentials.<key>}}, generated data as {{data.<fixture>.<field>}}, and a per-run id as {{run.shortId}}.

projectId.description: Assign to this project id, or null for account-level. Takes precedence over `project`.

project.description: Resolve a project by id, name, or "none". Used only when projectId is omitted; auto-picks if you have exactly one project.

agentType.description: functional | accessibility | uiux | exploratory | performance | security

runDevicesInParallel.description: Run selected devices in parallel instead of sequentially (needs >1 device).

headers.description: HTTP headers added to the browser's requests. Without `hosts` a header goes only to the site under test and its subdomains. `hosts` (array or comma string, max 20) sends it ONLY to those: "*" every host, "*.example.com" domain + subdomains, "api.example.com" exact host, "host:port".

preSteps.description: Run other plans first (by id or by name), sharing browser state.

tools.name: update_test_plan
tools.description: Edit an existing plan you own. Only the fields you pass change (partial update). Editable: name, prompt, testType, agentType, devices, paused, runDevicesInParallel, projectId, headers. Labels are edited with update_plan_labels (add/remove); pre-steps and cookies are not editable here (use the dashboard). Changing the prompt marks any saved script stale. Find the id with list_test_plans.

agentType.description: functional | accessibility | uiux | exploratory | performance | security

projectId.description: Move to this project id, or null for account-level.

headers.description: REPLACES the plan's whole header list (null or [] clears it). Without `hosts` a header goes only to the site under test and its subdomains; `hosts` (array or comma string, max 20) sends it ONLY to those: "*", "*.example.com", "api.example.com", "host:port".

tools.name: delete_test_plan
tools.description: Soft-delete a plan you own. Reversible server-side (run history is kept) and the deletion is recorded in the account's audit log. Find the id with list_test_plans.

tools.name: list_projects
tools.description: List the account's projects (id, name).

tools.name: list_schedules
tools.description: List the account's schedules: cadence (cron), enabled state, and what each runs - explicit test plans and/or whole projects (a project link runs ALL of the project's live plans at fire time, CI-style).

tools.name: update_schedule
tools.description: Update a schedule you own; only the fields you pass change. projectIds REPLACES the project links (each linked project runs all its live plans at fire time; [] clears); testPlanIds REPLACES the explicit plan links ([] clears). A schedule must keep at least one plan or project link. environmentName null = each plan uses its project's default env.

tools.name: set_credential
tools.description: Create or update an account credential, referenced in prompts/cookies/headers as {{credentials.<key>}}. Values are stored encrypted and never returned. Pass env to set a per-environment override on an existing key: runs against that environment name use the override, every other env uses the default value.

key.description: Starts with a letter; letters/digits/underscores; <=50 chars.

env.description: Environment name (e.g. staging) to set this value as an override for. The key must already have a default value.

tools.name: list_credentials
tools.description: List credential keys for the account, with the environment names of any per-env overrides. Values are never returned.

tools.name: list_labels
tools.description: List the account's labels and how many plans carry each.

tools.name: create_label
tools.description: Create (or fetch) a label by name. Labels are also auto-created when a plan references them.

tools.name: update_plan_labels
tools.description: Attach or detach labels on an EXISTING test plan (delta semantics, not replace). Names in `add` are get-or-created; names/ids in `remove` that aren't attached are a no-op. Returns the plan's resulting label set plus the net change. To set labels when first creating a plan, pass `labels` to create_test_plan instead.

add.description: Label names (created if new) or ids to attach.

remove.description: Label names or ids to detach (existing only; unknown/unattached is a no-op).

tools.name: get_preferences
tools.description: Read the account's testing preferences: autoUpgradeEnabled (retry a failed Quick Test with the Deep Test model), scriptRetryOnFailure (0-5 auto-retries for failed script runs), autoFixFlaky (AI repairs a flaky/regressed saved Playwright script, verifying before promoting), and the auto-fix label scope (autoFixLabelMode all/include/exclude + autoFixLabels: which plans auto-fix may touch, by label). Script-run settings do not affect AI runs.

tools.name: set_preferences
tools.description: Update one or more account testing preferences. Only the fields you pass change. autoFixFlaky enables automatic AI repair of flaky/regressed script runs (script runs only; verify-before-promote; billed like Refine). autoFixLabelMode + autoFixLabelNames scope auto-fix by plan label: 'include' fixes only plans carrying one of the labels, 'exclude' never fixes plans carrying one (e.g. an 'in-development' label), 'all' clears the filter (pass no names with it). include/exclude requires autoFixLabelNames IN THE SAME CALL: 1-10 EXISTING label names (never auto-created).

autoUpgradeEnabled.description: Retry a failed Quick Test with the more capable Deep Test model.

scriptRetryOnFailure.description: Number of automatic retries for a failed script run (0 disables). Script runs only.

autoFixFlaky.description: Let AI fix a flaky or newly-failing saved Playwright script automatically. Script runs only.

autoFixLabelMode.description: Label scope for auto-fix: 'all' (no filter), 'include' (only plans with one of autoFixLabelNames), 'exclude' (never those plans).

autoFixLabelNames.description: Existing label names the mode applies to (1-10). Required, in the same call, when autoFixLabelMode is include/exclude.

tools.name: list_data_fixtures
tools.description: List the account's test data: user-defined data fixtures (referenced as {{data.<fixture>.<field>}}), the built-in file fixtures for upload steps (referenced as {{file.<name>}}, e.g. {{file.pdf}} or {{file.png.5mb}}), AND the account's own uploaded custom files (referenced as {{file.custom.<key>}}). Omit project args for account-level fixtures; pass projectId (or project by id/name) to list a project's fixtures.

projectId.description: List this project id's fixtures. Takes precedence over `project`; omit for account-level.

project.description: List a project by id or name. Used only when projectId is omitted; no auto-pick.

tools.name: create_data_fixture
tools.description: Create a reusable data fixture for generated test data, referenced as {{data.<fixture>.<field>}}. Static fields carry a literal `value`; dynamic fields roll a fresh `value` per run from a `generator` (e.g. internet.email, person.firstName). Use the `examples` tool for the full generator list. Omit project args for an account-level fixture (visible to every project); pass projectId (or project by id/name) to scope it to one project.

key.description: Starts with a letter; letters/digits/underscores; <=50 chars.

projectId.description: Scope to this project id, or null/omit for account-level. Takes precedence over `project`.

project.description: Scope to a project by id or name. Used only when projectId is omitted; no auto-pick.

tools.name: get_script
tools.description: Download a plan's active Playwright script (uploaded or generated) so you can read or edit it, then re-upload with upload_script.

device.description: Defaults to the plan's first configured device.

out.description: Server-local path to write the script to (otherwise it's returned inline).

tools.name: script_status
tools.description: Check which saved Playwright scripts are outdated: a plan edited after its script was saved still runs the OLD script, and the plan keeps passing while testing stale behavior. Omit planId to audit every plan in the account in one call (the 'is my suite clean?' check). Reports state only - use get_script to read the source.

planId.description: Audit one plan. Omit to audit every plan in the account.

tools.name: upload_script
tools.description: Upload a local Playwright .spec.ts for a plan, skipping paid AI generation. The server validates it (allow-list + intent review) and stores it as the plan's saved script. On rejection the per-line issues are returned. Idempotent (upsert): re-running overwrites, never duplicates.

script.description: Full Playwright .spec.ts source. Provide this or `file`.

file.description: Server-local path to read the .spec.ts from. Used if `script` is omitted.

device.description: Defaults to the plan's first configured device.

tools.name: list_recordings
tools.description: List flows the user captured with the Test-Lab.ai Chrome extension's Record mode (id, name, step count, screenshots/video, draft/converted status). Start here when asked to turn a recording into a test plan or script.

tools.name: get_recording
tools.description: Fetch one recording: the raw captured actions (clicks, fills, navigations, asserts, with locator candidates and secret field refs), a deterministic draft test-plan prompt, and (with includeScript) a generated Playwright script in the uploaded-script format. THIS is the input for turning a recording into a proper test: review the actions, refine the draft prompt into a clean user-journey spec (drop noise, name the intent, keep {{credentials.*}} tokens), then create_test_plan with it - and optionally refine the generated script and upload_script to attach it to that plan. For an unreviewed 1:1 conversion use convert_recording instead.

includeScript.description: Also return the generated Playwright script (uploaded-script format).

tools.name: convert_recording
tools.description: Create a test plan from a recording 1:1 (deterministic, no review): the numbered draft prompt becomes the plan prompt as-is. One-shot per recording (409 once converted). When the user wants a PROPER reviewed plan, prefer get_recording + create_test_plan so you can refine the prompt first; use this for a quick as-recorded plan. credentialMap renames secret refs (e.g. {"secret-1": "staging_password"}).

name.description: Plan name (defaults to the recording's name).

projectId.description: Project to file the plan under; null for account-level.

tools.name: import_bundle
tools.description: Create credentials, labels, data fixtures, and plans in one go (created in dependency order; plans are topo-sorted so pre-step refs are created first). Provide `bundle` (inline) and/or `path` (a server-local .json file or directory of *.json). Use dryRun:true to validate and preview the creation order without writing.

bundle.description: Inline { credentials?, labels?, fixtures?, plans? }, an array of plans, or a single plan object.

path.description: Server-local path to a .json file or a directory of *.json files.

project.description: Assign imported plans to a project by id/name, or "none". Auto-picked if you have exactly one project.

tools.name: run_tests
tools.description: Trigger test runs. Provide exactly one selector: testPlanIds, projectId, or label. Returns one job per plan with its jobId and a results URL. Running tests consumes credits on pay-as-you-go accounts.

testPlanIds.description: An array of plan ids, or a comma-separated string.

projectId.description: Run all plans in this project.

label.description: Run all plans carrying this label.

env.description: Environment name; omit to use each project's default env.

buildId.description: CI build id (letters, numbers, dash, underscore, dot).

preferScript.description: Use saved/uploaded scripts instead of AI generation where available.

device.description: Run a single device (e.g. "iPhone 15 Pro"), validated against each plan's device list. Omit to fan out to EVERY device the plan configures (a plan with desktop + mobile runs both).

triggerPipelinePreSteps.description: Also run plans that are pipeline pre-steps (skipped by default in batch runs).

tunnelMode.description: Route browser traffic through this account's authorized extension tunnel.

cookies.description: Runtime cookies, merged over project + plan cookies.

headers.description: Runtime HTTP headers for this run only (e.g. a short-lived bypass token minted in CI), merged over environment + plan headers (runtime wins on the same name). Not stored. Without `hosts` a header goes only to the site under test and its subdomains; `hosts` (array or comma string, max 20) sends it ONLY to those: "*", "*.example.com", "api.example.com", "host:port".

tools.name: get_run
tools.description: Read a run's status, the failure error (the SAME text the Slack/webhook notifications print), and the per-step results by jobId (the jobId comes from run_tests). This is how you learn WHY a test failed so you can fix it - `run_tests` only triggers a run, this reads the outcome. Set wait:true to poll until the run reaches a terminal state (completed/failed/timeout/...); if it doesn't finish within timeoutSeconds you get an error result (call get_run again). Prefer a modest timeoutSeconds and re-call if still running, since a long synchronous wait can exceed your MCP client's request timeout. For a pipeline run it also returns the sibling steps and the first failing step.

jobId.description: The run/job id returned by run_tests.

wait.description: Poll until the run finishes (reaches a terminal state) before returning.

timeoutSeconds.description: Max seconds to wait when wait:true (default 600).

tools.name: list_runs
tools.description: List recent runs for the account (newest first), optionally filtered by planId. Returns lean rows (jobId + status) to then read one in full with get_run.

planId.description: Only runs of this test plan.

tools.name: examples
tools.description: Print the full copy-pasteable JSON reference for every resource (credentials, labels, data fixtures, plans, pre-steps, import bundles) and the reference syntax. Read this before create_test_plan / create_data_fixture / import_bundle when unsure of a shape.
